Roux-en-Y gastric bypass is a promising option for the long-term management of type 2 diabetes. While it may not fully cure the condition, research suggests that it can improve or even cure selected cases of type 1 diabetes when performed early in the disease. However, further studies are needed to confirm these findings.

The procedure has been shown to have potential benefits for patients with complex coronary lesions, such as bifurcation and ostial lesions, which are more common in diabetic individuals. This may help explain the poorer prognosis of coronary artery disease among diabetic patients.

In terms of pancreas retransplantation, a second chance for diabetic patients, Roux-en-Y gastric bypass is considered a safe procedure with acceptable graft survival rates. While there is limited evidence to support its use as a primary treatment option, it may be proposed in cases where the primary graft has failed or cannot be retained.

Regarding dietary habits among European individuals with type 1 diabetes, research suggests that they often consume a high-atherogenic diet, which can have negative effects on cardiovascular health. However, nutrition education is crucial to encourage healthier eating habits and reduce saturated fat and dietary fiber intake.

Finally, gastric electrical stimulation (GES) has been found to be more effective in improving long-term gastrointestinal symptoms, healthcare resources, and quality of life compared to standard pharmacologic therapy in patients with gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD). Certain high-risk patients may benefit from this treatment option.
